requested_by: Priya Okafor, IT Service Desk Manager, Harrowgate Instruments
title: Validate HR profile changes, review group rules and answer group membership tickets
situation: Harrowgate Instruments uses Okta Identity Engine as its identity provider, and apps are assigned to groups, so a person in the wrong group gets the wrong apps. HR sent 10 profile requests (new hires and changes) for Universal Directory, the identity team keeps 8 group rules written in Okta Expression Language, and the service desk has 14 tickets asking why someone is, or is not, in a group.
your_task: Check each profile request against the profile schema (the Okta base attributes plus the custom attributes businessUnit, badgeNumber, remoteWorker and certifications) and mark it ACCEPTED or REJECTED with the reason: unknown attribute, wrong data type, missing required attribute or unknown user.

Apply the accepted requests, then review every group rule: is it active, can its expression be read, and are its target groups ones a rule may populate (Okta groups and Active Directory groups, but never admin groups)?
Work out the resulting group memberships from the active rules, their exclude lists and the manually added members, remembering that deactivated users keep the memberships they already have.
For each ticket give the cause: RULE_MATCHED, RULE_INACTIVE, ATTRIBUTE_MISMATCH, USER_EXCLUDED, MANUAL_ASSIGNMENT, USER_NOT_ACTIVE or NO_RULE.
why_it_matters: Group rules decide app access for most of the company. A lower-case department value, an attribute name typed in the wrong case or a rule left inactive silently keeps people out of the apps they need, while a forgotten manual member, or a deactivated user who still sits in groups, keeps access that should be reviewed.
done_when: All 10 profile requests are ACCEPTED or REJECTED with the reason.
All 8 group rules are marked OK, INACTIVE, UNPARSEABLE or INVALID_TARGET.
The membership of every group is listed.
All 14 tickets have a cause and a reason the service desk can pass on.

glossary.Okta Identity Engine (OIE): The current Okta platform that runs sign-in, policies and the user directory.
glossary.Universal Directory: Okta's directory of user profiles, holding the base attributes and any custom attributes.
glossary.Custom attribute: A profile attribute added by an administrator in the Profile Editor, with a fixed data type.
glossary.Okta Expression Language (OEL): The expression syntax used in group rules, for example user.department == "Sales".
glossary.Group rule: A condition that adds every matching user to one or more Okta groups automatically.
glossary.Human resources (HR): The team, and its system, that is the source of employee data such as department and title.
glossary.Admin group: A group that holds an Okta administrator role; group rules can't add users to it.
glossary.Active Directory (AD) group: A group in Microsoft's on-premises directory; Okta group rules can populate it from user attributes through the AD integration.
glossary.Deactivated user: A user whose status is DEPROVISIONED: app assignments are removed, group memberships stay until the user is deleted, and group rules stop evaluating them.

talking_point: Validated 10 HR profile requests in Okta Universal Directory (4 accepted, 6 rejected for an unknown attribute, wrong data types, missing required attributes or an unknown user), found 3 of 8 group rules needing attention (one inactive, one targeting an admin group and one that could not be parsed), and closed 14 group membership tickets, 3 of them caused by attribute mismatches such as a lower-case department and 2 by deactivated users, who keep their group memberships until deleted.
